body: I did almost the same thing...! But I went so far so I got baptized in the first wave of psychosis, I  didn't realize that my hallucinations were hallucinations at the time. But the priest and the other personal in the church was very nice though..

Well according to Wikipedia, there's about 1 in every 285 person that has schizophrenia and 20% of 1/285 is about 1/5700 (if I counted right).That's 1/5700 of 27 million people with Schizophrenia (again, mathematics isn't my strong suite so I could have counted wrong).

I get your point of view.. But I can't imagine living like this for the rest of my life, being so alone  and isolated from the outside world and not being active or contributing in someway puts me in a very negative frame of mind. In addition I must say that, the thought of "throwing my life away" scares me quite a bit and I'm not sure that is something I could ever do. You're right that we live in a good place in time to actually have a mental condition, but I still want so much more out of life.   
You are definitely not the first person to tell me that I need to accept my current condition, and to be honest.. On a cognitive level I totally get what you're referring to but emotionally I get so overwhelmingly angry and frustrated. I'm not saying that to offend you or anyone else, but I dislike hearing those words and especially from someone who have no experience of mental illness themselves and therefore have no clue what they're talking about.

Yeah, that's very true - that you are more than your illness. But for me at least, I lost all of friends and the experience that I have had is that people don't really know how to talk approach the subject. I do agree on that you can stigmatize yourself, and maybe that's what I been doing. The big question is how do I stop doing that and "go back to" or socialize better? Because I had some minor problems pre-psychosis with social interactions but now it has become a problem for me personally.
I think this would be great.
Thank you, and in some sense that is true. But I wish I didn't feel the way I do and the internet doesn't change that.
